# ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io Daily Update (May 8, 2026)
## OVERVIEW 
Today's development focused on in-depth investigations into existing issues, particularly around flaky tests and brotli decompression divergences, with significant progress made in understanding root causes and proposing solutions.

## KEY TECHNICAL DEVELOPMENTS

No new features, bug fixes, code refactoring, documentation enhancements, or tests were added today.

## NEWLY OPENED PULL REQUESTS
No new pull requests were opened today.

## CLOSED ISSUES
No issues were closed today.

## NEW ISSUES
No new issues were opened today.

## ACTIVE ISSUES

### Flaky Test Investigation: `TestFlashblocksTransfer`
Discussion on [#19934](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/19934) continued with a detailed investigation into the `TestFlashblocksTransfer` flake. A new draft PR (ethereum-optimism/optimism#20600) was opened to address the failure mode, restructuring the test into two sequential phases (60s tx-confirmation, 30s flashblock-observation) with improved diagnostics. The investigation revealed that `op-rbuilder` produced zero flashblocks during the test run, leading to a misleading error message and a 30-minute hang. The proposed changes aim to make failures faster (~90s) and more unambiguous, distinguishing between "tx never confirmed," "op-rbuilder published zero flashblocks," or "flashblocks for other blocks but not the inclusion block." The underlying `op-rbuilder` flashblock-emission bug remains to be fixed in a separate effort.

### Kona and op-node Brotli Divergence
Significant progress was made in understanding the divergence between Kona and op-node regarding brotli channels in [#19333](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/19333). A previous correction to the investigation revealed that both Go libraries (`andybalholm/brotli` and `google/brotli` cgo) behave identically and match the reference C implementation. The dominant cause of divergence was identified as a 4-line wrapper bug in Kona's `decompress_brotli` function, which incorrectly handled `NeedsMoreInput` when `available_out` was also zero, leading to partial buffer returns. Fixing this wrapper bug is expected to eliminate 95% of the divergences. Further investigation is planned for the remaining 11 corruption-only divergences, which are genuine differences between the Rust crate and Go's behavior on corrupted inputs. A library swap for Kona's brotli decoder is no longer deemed necessary.

### Safedb Proof Requirements
Discussion on [#20593](https://github.com/ethereum-optimism/ethereum-optimism.github.io/issues/20593) highlighted the need to review how `op-supernode` utilizes the safe head database. It was noted that `op-supernode` is currently the primary use case for the safe head database, and its necessity might diminish once proofs transition to ZK. The discussion also touched upon the theoretical use case of challenging proposals made too early before batch data landed on L1, but concluded that as long as the output root is from the canonical chain, the safe head database might not be needed.
